query: Help me understand the key points in this table — what should I concentrate on?

per_column.name: complaint_category
per_column.rationale: Rather than isolating one aspect of service quality, this is a catch-all taxonomy of failure types spanning staff, delays, billing, food, seat, baggage, etc. It re-slices the whole concept and overlaps with nearly every other facet column, so it functions as a compressed restatement of the whole rather than a single MECE part.

per_column.name: staff_attitude_judgment
per_column.rationale: Interpersonal/staff service is a genuine constitutive aspect of airline service quality — a clean 'aspect of' the concept.

per_column.name: food_quality_judgment
per_column.rationale: Catering/food quality is a legitimate constitutive facet of the in-flight service experience.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: How delays/cancellations are handled is a real service-delivery aspect of quality, distinct from static product facets.

per_column.name: compensation_resolution_outcome
per_column.rationale: Complaint resolution / remediation is a constitutive facet of service recovery, though it partly overlaps with disruption_handling_quality when disruptions drive the compensation.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Perceived value is a recognized dimension of service quality (and mirrors the original Value For Money rating), so it counts as a facet, albeit an evaluative/summary one that risks overlapping the overall judgment.

per_column.name: service_consistency_concern
per_column.rationale: Reliability/consistency is a core SERVQUAL-style dimension of service quality — an aspect of the concept.

per_column.name: repeat_or_loyalty_signal
per_column.rationale: Loyalty/repeat intention is a downstream OUTCOME of service quality, not a part of it. It is predicted by quality rather than constituting it.

per_column.name: special_needs_handling
per_column.rationale: Handling of special assistance/accessibility is a specific, non-overlapping constitutive aspect of the service experience.

judge.rationale: Most added columns are genuine facets (staff, food, disruption handling, resolution, value, consistency, special needs). However MECE is weakened on both axes. Mutual exclusivity: complaint_category is a whole-concept re-slice that overlaps almost every other facet, and disruption_handling_quality vs compensation_resolution_outcome overlap around service recovery, while value_for_money is an evaluative summary that partly duplicates the overall judgment. Two columns are not facets at all: complaint_category (restatement) and repeat_or_loyalty_signal (downstream outcome). Exhaustiveness: coverage is decent but omits key constitutive aspects present even in the source table — seat/cabin comfort as a product dimension, inflight entertainment reliability (only appears as a complaint bucket), booking/check-in/ground process, and cleanliness/punctuality, so the facet set does not fully cover the concept's main aspects.
